findings.title: Reserve existing Owned termination allowance before waiting through the final windows
findings.effect: If the worker returns service-first-result before275 but hangs during cleanup, wait_worker waits until310 before failing. cleanup_no_listener then has at most5 seconds left to315. The reused PrivateIO terminate wrapper requires full_ns=10000000000 before entering the unchanged termination function, so it refuses to terminate every still-live registered process. A reader hanging through315 is worse: cleanup_no_listener pre-check throws before Owned.cleanup is entered at all. Thus failure is correctly classified but the owned worker/reader may remain alive with open logs after the root exits. This violates the practical cleanup expectation; a failed verdict alone is not process cleanup.

findings.remedy: Schedule failure cleanup early enough to retain the unchanged Owned termination allowance plus required discovery/wait/final-proof time within the original315 origin. Do not extend deadlines or add a new killer. If preserving the full consumer windows cannot coexist with that existing helper, explicitly record the incompatibility as blocking instead of proposing runtime. Add a synthetic contract exercising the actual reused Deadline/PrivateIO with a still-live owned member near310 and a reader stall; demonstrate cleanup is entered with sufficient original budget and closes logs.
